note: error_page shows a friendly, customizable page on fatal errors/exceptions. It has NO admin UI, NO config entities, NO Drush, NO permissions, NO plugins (configure=null, provides_config_schema=false); it is configured only via $settings['error_page'] in settings.php. Because the shared site's real settings.php must stay untouched, the medium cases introspect the module's live container footprint (its registered final-exception subscriber service error_page.exception_subscriber => ErrorPageFinalExceptionSubscriber, and the priority -255 that class subscribes at on KernelEvents::EXCEPTION), and the hard cases have the agent write the correct settings.php directives into a dedicated, deletable scratch snippet file (web/sites/default/settings.error_page_*.eval.php) which the verify greps and the reset deletes — keeping the real settings.php safe while still checking live filesystem state the agent produced. NOTE: error_page also swaps core's 'exception.logger' class (ErrorPageServiceProvider), but on THIS site simple_oauth also swaps that service and wins, so the mediums deliberately target error_page's own subscriber service (which is unambiguously active) rather than the shared exception.logger. All facts are grounded in src/ (ErrorPageFinalExceptionSubscriber priority -255; ErrorPageErrorHandler::handleError/handleException; ErrorPagePhpErrorLogger log method/destination) and README.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal contrib module error_page. Enabling it already replaces the page for uncaught exceptions, but I also want it to catch fatal and user-level PHP errors. What exactly do I add to settings.php to do that?
evals.expected_output: In settings.php register the module's handlers: set_error_handler(['Drupal\error_page\ErrorPageErrorHandler', 'handleError']); and set_exception_handler(['Drupal\error_page\ErrorPageErrorHandler', 'handleException']);. (If not using Composer autoloading, first require_once the ErrorPageErrorHandler.php file.)

evals.prompt: How do I turn off the per-error UUID in the Drupal error_page module, and where is that configured? Is there an admin form for it?
evals.expected_output: error_page has no admin form (configure=null); everything is in settings.php. Set $settings['error_page']['uuid'] = FALSE; to disable UUID generation. It defaults to TRUE.

evals.prompt: How can I customize the look/wording of the friendly page that Drupal's error_page module shows? Which files and which placeholder tokens are involved, and how do I point the module at my copies?
evals.expected_output: Copy markup/error_page.html (full page) and/or markup/error_message.html (inline message) somewhere (ideally outside the web root), edit them using the tokens {{ uuid }}, {{ base_path }} and {{ error_report }}, and set $settings['error_page']['template_dir'] to that directory. Output is plain HTML with strtr() token replacement, not Twig.

evals.prompt: On this running Drupal site the error_page module is enabled. It renders the friendly page for uncaught exceptions via its own event subscriber service. Inspect the live site and tell me the service id error_page registers for this, and the class that service instantiates.
evals.expected_output: Service id error_page.exception_subscriber, class Drupal\error_page\EventSubscriber\ErrorPageFinalExceptionSubscriber. Discoverable with: drush php:eval "echo get_class(\Drupal::service('error_page.exception_subscriber'));".

evals.prompt: error_page's exception subscriber has to run just before core's FinalExceptionSubscriber so it can render its own page and stop the event. On this live site, inspect error_page's subscriber and tell me the priority it registers for on the KernelEvents::EXCEPTION event.
evals.expected_output: It subscribes to KernelEvents::EXCEPTION at priority -255 (core FinalExceptionSubscriber is -256). Discoverable with: drush php:eval "var_export(\Drupal\error_page\EventSubscriber\ErrorPageFinalExceptionSubscriber::getSubscribedEvents());".

evals.prompt: error_page is configured in settings.php. To keep this shared site's real settings.php untouched, write the exact settings.php PHP directives that register error_page's fatal-error and exception handlers into the file web/sites/default/settings.error_page_handlers.eval.php (create it). It must register both the error handler and the exception handler pointing at the module's ErrorPageErrorHandler class.

I want error_page to write fatal-error details to a log file via PHP's error_log(). Without touching this shared site's real settings.php, write the correct settings.php directives into the file web/sites/default/settings.error_page_log.eval.php (create it): set the error_page log method to 3 (log to file) and give it a destination file.
evals.expected_output: The file sets $settings['error_page']['log']['method'] = 3; and $settings['error_page']['log']['destination'] = 'temporary://error_log.txt'; (any destination path is fine).
